title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The child device (EE2) shares its live GPS coordinates with the backend (P1) without explicit consent or a clear purpose for the data, creating a risk of location tracking.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The backend (P1) receives and stores the GPS coordinates, which may be used to track the child's location over time, potentially violating privacy expectations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: The mobile app (P1) shares location data with the backend (P1) without explicit user consent or a valid privacy policy, allowing the backend to access sensitive location information.

title: Data Exfiltration or Misuse
description: The Location History Store (DS1) receives the location data and stores it in a way that allows for unauthorized access, sharing, or deletion by unauthorized parties.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app (P1) shares raw location coordinates with the backend (P1) without any user consent or explicit permission to share this sensitive personal information.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The mobile app (P1) processes the raw location data by sending it to the backend, which may store it indefinitely or use it for analytics without a clear purpose.

title: Geofencing Logic Error
description: The geofencing engine (P2) processes the incoming location data by comparing it against a database of known locations, which may incorrectly flag a user as being in a restricted zone.

title: Unauthorized Access to Family Account
description: The source element (DataStore) shares data (family account details) with the destination element (Geofencing Engine) without explicit, granular permission controls. This allows the destination to access sensitive personal data (e.g., family members, addresses) that the source owner may not intend to be publicly or broadly shared.
assumptions: The system assumes the DataStore owner has broad permissions to share account data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the DataStore owner has specific granular permissions for 'family' data versus 'public' data.

title: Data Processing for Geofencing
description: The destination element (Geofencing Engine) processes the shared data by performing geofencing logic. This processing step may infer or aggregate data about the family members (e.g., 'home' zone) to trigger alerts, which could be used to identify or track the family members based on their location.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine assumes the family members are the primary entities of interest for the alert.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the processing logic is designed to identify individuals or just aggregate location data.

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: The child element (P2) shares sensitive geofencing data (arrival/departure notifications) with the parent (EE1) without explicit, granular authorization for the parent to access this specific data. This creates a risk that the parent could access data it is not authorized to see, potentially violating the principle of least privilege.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE1) is not explicitly granted the right to view the specific data flow from P2.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The parent element (EE1) receives the geofencing notifications and processes them in a way that causes a privacy threat. For example, the parent might aggregate, store, or use this data for its own analytics or decision-making without a clear, documented purpose, or it might use the data to identify the parent's own users in a way that is not intended.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE1) does not have a clear, documented purpose for processing this specific data flow.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity information (e.g., name, DOB, school) with the mobile app backend (P1) during the registration process. This creates a risk that the parent's identity is exposed to the backend, potentially allowing the backend to link or identify the parent with other data.
assumptions: The parent entity is aware of its identity and is willing to share it.

title: Data Usage for Linking
description: The parent entity shares its identity data with the backend, which may use this data to link or identify the parent with other entities or data sets not explicitly requested.
assumptions: The backend has the capability to perform linking or identification operations.

title: Data Processing for Geofencing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the parent's identity data and uses it to define geofence zones. This processing may involve storing or processing the identity data in a way that causes a threat, such as making the identity data available for geofencing logic.
assumptions: The backend has the capability to define geofence zones using the received identity data.

title: Data Collection
description: The mobile app collects account, child profile, and geofence zone data from the user without explicit, informed consent.
assumptions: The app assumes the user has granted necessary permissions.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the app provides a clear, granular consent mechanism for each data type.

title: Data Inference
description: The app may infer sensitive information about the child's location or family status from the geofence zone data.
assumptions: The app's data processing logic allows for such inference.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the app's specific data processing logic supports this inference.

title: Data Storage
description: The app stores the collected data in a way that could be used to identify the child or family members.
assumptions: The app does not implement robust data minimization or anonymization.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the app's storage implementation includes appropriate safeguards.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow transmits metadata about the parties involved (e.g., app ID, user ID, device ID) which could be used to link or identify the user and the child.
assumptions: The app transmits standard metadata fields without obfuscation.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the app transmits additional identifying metadata beyond standard fields.

title: Data Processing
description: The data store processes the received data in a way that could reveal sensitive information about the child or family.
assumptions: The store does not apply any additional filtering or masking.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the store applies any additional filtering or masking.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its child's location data with the mobile app backend without explicit consent or a valid legal basis for sharing personal location information.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) processes the parent's request to view location history, which may involve storing, aggregating, or re-identifying the parent's location data.

title: Location History Exposure
description: The source element (DataStore) shares location history data with the backend process. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to the recipient, potentially allowing the recipient to link or identify the data owner (the parent) with the data itself.
assumptions: The parent application has access to the backend API and the data is not encrypted or anonymized before transmission.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The destination element (Process) receives the location history data and processes it to serve the parent's map/history view. This action causes the threat because the data is stored and potentially used for personalization or profiling, which can lead to re-identification of the data owner.
assumptions: The backend process does not perform any additional data minimization or anonymization steps before serving the data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity with the mobile app backend (P1) to facilitate the invitation process. This disclosure allows the backend to identify the parent as a specific individual, which is necessary for the invitation but creates a privacy risk if the parent's identity is not adequately protected or if the backend uses this identity for other purposes.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the parent's identity and location data. The backend processes this data to generate the invitation and stores it. This processing may involve aggregating location data from multiple parents or storing it in a way that allows for future access or profiling, which poses a privacy risk.

title: Unauthorized Access to Live Location Data
description: The backend process (P1) shares the child's live location data with the secondary guardian (EE3) without explicit, granular consent for this specific purpose. This creates a risk that the guardian could access, misuse, or leak the live location data.
assumptions: The backend process has the capability to share live location data.
uncertainty_note: Confident that the backend shares data, but the specific granularity of consent for live location sharing is not explicitly detailed in the flow description.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing by Secondary Guardian
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) receives the live location data and may process it in ways that cause privacy threats, such as storing it, sharing it with third parties, or using it for non-consensual purposes.
assumptions: The secondary guardian has the capability to process the received data.
uncertainty_note: Confident that the guardian processes data, but the specific risks of misuse are not fully detailed.

title: Data Sharing of Sensitive Usage Data
description: The source element (Backend) shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with an external advertising/analytics partner. This data is highly sensitive as it contains personally identifiable information (PII) and behavioral data that could be used to identify, track, and profile users across the ecosystem.
assumptions: The backend system has the necessary technical capability to transmit this data securely, but the act of sharing itself exposes the data to potential misuse.

title: Data-Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow itself carries meta-data about the parties involved (Backend and EE4). This metadata, such as the names of the entities or the specific data types being exchanged, can be used to link or identify the parties, even if the actual data payload is encrypted.
assumptions: The metadata is not encrypted or obfuscated in a way that prevents third parties from identifying the source and destination entities.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing by Partner
description: The destination element (Advertising/Analytics Partner) receives the data and processes it in a way that causes a threat. The partner may use the data for targeted advertising, which could lead to the collection of additional PII or the creation of profiles that are not authorized by the user.
assumptions: The partner's internal systems are not sufficiently secured to prevent unauthorized access or misuse of the shared analytics data.

title: Location Disclosure
description: The child entity (EE2) shares its current location with the parent entity (P1) via a manual check-in/SOS message. This action exposes the child's precise location to the parent, potentially enabling the parent to track or monitor the child's movements.
assumptions: The child is aware of the parent's identity and intent to share location data.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The parent entity (P1) receives the location data and stores it in a way that allows for future tracking or profiling of the child. This processing may involve aggregating location data over time or correlating it with other user data.
assumptions: The parent entity has the capability to store and process the received location data.
